full_judgment: 44. There are two modes for appointment of a Director of a private Company. The subscribers of the memorandum shall be deemed to be the directors of a company as per clause (a) to section 91(1) of the Act of 1994, The other manner of appointment is by way of election in the Annual General Meeting (AGM). And the other mode is the filling up of the casual vacancy on the retirement of a director. The appellants not being the subscribers of the company, the first clause is not applicable to them. The positive case of the Bangladesh Bank is that the appellants acquired shares and then became directors of the company, therefore, clause (c) to section 91(1) of Act, 1994 is attracted in their case. So, election by the, members in AGM as contended by the learned counsel for the appellants is not necessary for them for such appointment. The Board has power to appoint a director and this power might be exercised notwithstanding that the strength of the Board had fallen below the minimum required and below the quorums prescribed by the articles. They filled up the casual vacancy of the Board of the defaulter company in accordance with law. Further, returns in form XII are required to be submitted by the company, which are kept with the office of Registrar, Joint Stock Companies which are public documents. There is presumption in favour of official acts being legal until contrary is proved. The official acts are presumed to be legally performed and where the jurisdiction of an officer is not questioned in the Court, it must be presumed that he acted within the jurisdiction. Therefore, this point merits no consideration.
